topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting it to histopathology practicals and outlining the day's learning outcomes on cellular transformation, oncogenes, and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the historical discovery of oncogenes from transforming tumor viruses and the laboratory assays used to test transforming activity in cells and animal models.

topics.label: Characteristics and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressor Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the classes of cancer-driving mutations and explain how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes regulate the cell cycle and exert dominant, recessive, or dominant-negative effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Genetic Instability and Multi-Step Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms causing sequence and chromosomal instability—including DNA repair failures, replication errors, and mitotic abnormalities—and how these drive multi-step carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predispositions and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how inherited mutations in gatekeeper and caretaker genes predispose individuals to cancer and how genetic instability influences tumor evolution and treatment response.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with an offer for questions, a book recommendation, and a preview of the upcoming lecture.
